title: Android manifest permissions vs third-party SDKs
subtitle: Latest analyzed build of 171 Android apps, 1 Nov 2026
selection: Every Android app with a the source tech-stack page, latest analyzed build each: 171 builds. v1 used only the 80 SDK-heaviest builds (31+ SDKs) from /tech-stack, which hid the 6 apps that request more permissions than Meta AI.
method: permissions = 'Permissions' count on each app's Android tech-stack page (permissions requested in the manifest). sdks = 'Third-party SDKs' count on the same page. One point per app.

x.label: Third-party SDKs detected in the build

permissions.meaning: Number of permissions declared in the analyzed build's AndroidManifest (as listed by the source).

biases.text: Declared, not granted: includes install-time 'normal' permissions and ones merged in from libraries; says nothing about what the app actually uses.
Alipay shows exactly 200 permissions and 200 native libs, and TikTok exactly 200 native libs: 200 may be a the source list cap, so Alipay's real count could be higher.
141 of 171 builds were analyzed in Jun 2026; current versions may differ.
the source's analyzed set (popular/tracked apps), not all of Google Play.

sdks.meaning: Third-party SDKs detected in the same build.

biases.text: Detection is 'observed' for 130 builds and 'lower bound' for 41; first-party code (e.g. Meta's own libraries in Facebook) is not a third-party SDK, so Facebook shows 2.

footnote: Source: {source}, 1 Nov 2026. Latest build of {n_rows} apps, not all of Google Play.
Permissions: declared in the manifest, not granted or used. Alipay's 200 may be a list cap.
SDKs: {n_observed} observed, {n_lower} a lower bound. {stale_count} builds older than 60 days (oldest {oldest}).
source_default: public Android app build analysis pages
